hero.caption: The office of the LeConte Lodge mountaintop "resort" near the summit of Mount Le Conte is the hub of activities both at the lodge and on the mountain. Customers at the lodge are offered numerous forms of non-electronic entertainment here, and many day-hikers use the office as a resting place before making the trek back down the mountain.

images.caption: Looking east from Myrtle Point, one of the four peaks of Mount Le Conte in the Great Smoky Mountains of Tennessee, located in the southeastern United States.  As the morning fog lifts, Mt. Guyot and the Eastern Smokies emerge to dominate the horizon.  The spine-like tree on the right is actually the top of a dead fraser fir in the foreground.

images.caption: The summit (High Top) of Mount Le Conte (6,593 ft/2,010m) in the Great Smoky Mountains of Tennessee, located in the southeastern United States.  A tradition among hikers is to deposit a rock on the pile, hearkening back to a Cherokee tradition that involves appeasing evil spirits.  The summit is located along the Boulevard Trail.
images.alt: The summit (High Top) of Mount Le Conte (6,593 ft/2,010m) in the Great Smoky Mountains of Tennessee, located in the southeastern United States.  A tradition among hikers is to deposit a rock on the pile, hearkening back to a Cherokee tradition that involves appeasing evil spirits.  The summit is located along the Boulevard Trail.

images.caption: The view looking east from the summit of Clingmans Dome in the Great Smoky Mountains of Tennessee and North Carolina, in the southeastern United States.  Mount Le Conte spans most of the photo on the right.  Sugarland Mountain spans the photo in the foreground.  The Tennessee Valley (Sevier Co. and Cocke Co.) are in the distance on the left.  On the Le Conte massif, Balsam Point is the summit at the far left.  West Point is right of center in the photograph, followed (to the right) by Cliff Top, High Top, and Myrtle Point.
images.alt: The view looking east from the summit of Clingmans Dome in the Great Smoky Mountains of Tennessee and North Carolina, in the southeastern United States.  Mount Le Conte spans most of the photo on the right.  Sugarland Mountain spans the photo in the foreground.  The Tennessee Valley (Sevier Co. and Cocke Co.) are in the distance on the left.  On the Le Conte massif, Balsam Point is the summit at the far left.  West Point is right of center in the photograph, followed (to the right) by Cliff Top, High Top, and Myrtle Point.
